coverageMatrix.completeness: Doxycycline provides complete coverage of the causative organism.
gaps: None for the primary pathogen — ensure careful skin exam to exclude scrub typhus (different epidemiological pattern, though same first-line treatment).

stewardship.deescalation: Not applicable — doxycycline is already the single most targeted agent. If the patient fails to improve within 48-72 hours, reconsider the diagnosis rather than escalating antibiotics.

drugs.route: Oral (or IV if unable to tolerate oral)
drugs.why: Doxycycline is first-line for all spotted fever group rickettsioses, with the same rapid, dramatic clinical response characteristic of rickettsial disease in general.

drugs.coverage: Reasonable alternative when tetracyclines are relatively contraindicated, though doxycycline remains preferred even in most pregnancy guidance given disease severity considerations — individualize per specialist input.

framework: Do not withhold empiric doxycycline pending serology in a clinically compatible presentation — early treatment significantly reduces morbidity, similar to scrub typhus.

Always perform a careful skin examination for an eschar — if found, this points more specifically to scrub typhus, though treatment (doxycycline) is the same either way, so this distinction matters more for epidemiological/public health purposes than immediate management.
Treat for the full course even after rapid defervescence, which is characteristic of rickettsial disease but does not justify a shortened course.

references: NCDC India Guidelines for Rickettsial Diseases
